title: Emergency Treatment of Asthma Exacerbations According to GINA Guidelines

notes.text: Asthma: inflammation and variable airflow
A concise, newly authored revision guide for this topic. Use the video for the instructor’s full explanation; these notes do not claim to transcribe it.
Variable expiratory airflow limitation is a defining physiologic feature of asthma.
Inhaled corticosteroid-containing treatment reduces exacerbation risk and is central to current GINA management.
Inhaler technique and adherence should be checked before escalating long-term treatment.
Severe exacerbation requires urgent assessment of respiratory effort, oxygenation, and response to therapy.

title: Mepolizumab & Reslizumab: Mechanism of Action, Therapeutic Uses and Adverse Effects

notes.text: Anti-IL-5 therapy
A concise, newly authored revision guide for this topic. Use the video for the instructor’s full explanation; these notes do not claim to transcribe it.
Interleukin-5 supports eosinophil growth and survival.
Mepolizumab and reslizumab target IL-5 in selected patients with severe eosinophilic asthma.
Phenotype assessment helps determine whether biologic treatment is appropriate.
Maintenance therapy is the role of these biologics; they are not rescue bronchodilators.

notes.text: Omalizumab
A concise, newly authored revision guide for this topic. Use the video for the instructor’s full explanation; these notes do not claim to transcribe it.
IgE is the target of omalizumab.
Allergic asthma is an established indication in appropriately selected patients.
Anaphylaxis is an important potential adverse reaction.
Biologic selection depends on disease phenotype and eligibility criteria.

title: Anti Leukotrienes (Montelukast, Zafirlukast & Zileuton): Mechanism of Action & Therapeutic Uses

notes.text: Leukotriene modifiers
A concise, newly authored revision guide for this topic. Use the video for the instructor’s full explanation; these notes do not claim to transcribe it.
Montelukast blocks the cysteinyl leukotriene receptor.
Zileuton inhibits 5-lipoxygenase and reduces leukotriene synthesis.
Bronchoconstriction and mucus production are effects of cysteinyl leukotrienes.
Neuropsychiatric effects are an important safety concern with montelukast.

title: Inhaled Corticosteroids (ICS): Mechanism of Action, Therapeutic Uses & Adverse Effects

notes.text: Inhaled corticosteroids
A concise, newly authored revision guide for this topic. Use the video for the instructor’s full explanation; these notes do not claim to transcribe it.
Airway inflammation is reduced by inhaled corticosteroids.
Oral candidiasis is a local adverse effect.
Mouth rinsing after use can help reduce local adverse effects.
Controller therapy reduces future risk; most inhaled steroid products alone do not provide rapid rescue bronchodilation.

title: Methylxanthines (Theophylline & Aminophylline): Mechanism of Action and Therapeutic Uses

notes.text: Methylxanthines
A concise, newly authored revision guide for this topic. Use the video for the instructor’s full explanation; these notes do not claim to transcribe it.
Theophylline has bronchodilator activity and a narrow therapeutic index.
Drug interactions can significantly alter theophylline concentrations.
Arrhythmias and seizures are serious manifestations of toxicity.
Concentration monitoring may be necessary when these medicines are used.

title: Ipratropium Bromide in Asthma Treatment: Mechanism of Action, Therapeutic Uses & Adverse Effects

notes.text: Ipratropium
A concise, newly authored revision guide for this topic. Use the video for the instructor’s full explanation; these notes do not claim to transcribe it.
Muscarinic receptor blockade reduces vagally mediated bronchoconstriction.
Ipratropium is a short-acting inhaled antimuscarinic.
Dry mouth is a common adverse effect.
Adjunct therapy with a short-acting beta agonist is useful in some acute severe asthma settings.

title: Beta 2 Adrenergic Agonists: Mechanism of Action, Therapeutic Uses and Adverse Effects

notes.text: Beta-2 agonists
A concise, newly authored revision guide for this topic. Use the video for the instructor’s full explanation; these notes do not claim to transcribe it.
Beta-2 receptor stimulation relaxes bronchial smooth muscle.
Cyclic AMP is an intracellular mediator of the bronchodilator response.
Tremor and tachycardia are recognized adverse effects.
Hypokalemia may occur through movement of potassium into cells.
